homonyms.basis: The census record carries no disambiguation field; its one negative tag holds the entity apart from its largest source ('NOT the Schoenberg Database itself: it aggregates SDBM with Bibale and the Bodleian's catalogue', PE-17). No card is a homonym. 'MMM' is the project's abbreviation and is not used as an alias (it is not in the archive's texts and is a common string). The MMM Semantic Portal, the MMM Knowledge Graph (the Zenodo dataset) and the MMM Data Model are parts of the entity, not senses of the name.
distinct_entities: Schoenberg Database of Manuscripts (SDBM; Penn, Schoenberg Institute for Manuscript Studies): a source the project aggregates and a distinct entity; built in parallel as the /non row schoenberg-database (datasets/negative-of-the-negative/v2/rows/schoenberg-database.json), its neighbour, which this row does not edit; the census relates them has_part / part_of
Bibale (IRHT-CNRS): a source the project aggregates
Medieval Manuscripts in Oxford Libraries (the Bodleian's catalogue; 'the Medieval Manuscripts Catalogue' on two cards)
Linked Data Finland (LDF.fi) and Sampo-UI (Aalto's Semantic Computing Research Group): the platform and framework that serve it
the CERL Portal and Digital Scriptorium (the earlier cross-searches its white paper names)
Arnold Schoenberg (the composer, in the archive's #1569), unrelated to the Schoenberg Database's name in this row's sense

captures.description: MAPPING MANUSCRIPT MIGRATIONS, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'an international digital humanities project that unites disparate historical records to trace the origins, movements, provenance, and ownership history of medieval and Renaissance manuscripts.' Scale ('over 215,000 historical manuscripts'), partners (Penn, Oxford, IRHT-CNRS, Aalto) and funding (the Trans-Atlantic Platform's Digging into Data Challenge), and the merged sources (the Schoenberg Database, Bibale, 'the Medieval Manuscripts Catalogue') as a linked open data knowledge graph, queryable through the portal and LDF.fi. Six cards: the GitHub page, the Journal of Open Humanities Data (2020), EADH, the University of San Diego, the Zenodo record of the knowledge graph, Goldsmiths Research Online.

atoms.evidence: A collaboration between the University of Pennsylvania, University of Oxford, Institut de recherche et d'histoire des textes (IRHT-CNRS), and Aalto University
